prompt: A different client's support tickets all arrive through a single email inbox already, with no fragmentation across channels. They ask for an AI chatbot to draft first-pass responses. Does the same objection from the lesson apply here?

options.text: Yes — a chatbot drafting first-pass responses still needs a triage/routing layer added first, the same way the fragmented case did
No — the fragmentation problem that made the chatbot premature in the lesson isn't present here, so the objection doesn't apply
Yes — a single consolidated inbox is itself a sign the client hasn't scaled enough to need this level of automation yet

hints: The lesson's objection was specific to a fragmentation problem, not to AI chatbots in general.
Check whether the actual condition that made the chatbot premature — multiple unconnected queues — exists in this new scenario.
explanation: The objection in the lesson wasn't 'chatbots are premature by default' — it was that a specific bottleneck (three fragmented, unconnected ticket channels) existed and the chatbot wouldn't touch it. Here, tickets already arrive through one consolidated channel, so that specific bottleneck doesn't exist, and there's no equivalent reason to delay the chatbot for integration work first. The skill is diagnosing the actual process each time, not applying a blanket rule.
